AUTONOMOUS SUPPLIER INVOICE PROCESSING AGENT
URL: https://hl-consulting.tech/knowledge-hub/en/journal/agent-factures-architecture.html
Published: 2026-05-29
================================================================

Designing the full architecture of an invoice agent (5 channels, line-by-line matching, 4 sub-agents, Teams actions) before writing a single line of code. Only touch Odoo once a week.

← Journal
Cobra · Multi-agent architecture design
Autonomous supplier invoice processing agent
Claude · Cobra · May 2026 · Cobra agenten-cours
Context
Hugo was manually processing every supplier invoice in Odoo: checking lines, adding WEEE/shipping/discounts, matching the VAT-inc total, confirming. The goal: only touch Odoo once a week for the SEPA batch — everything else happens in Teams.
What was built (design)
- Mapping of 5 input channels + identification of Cobra's two main ones: comptabilite@cobra.fr and PO via chatter
- Distinction between accounting families: merchandise (PO-linked, 607xxx) vs. overheads (6xxxx)
- Line-by-line matching: identification hierarchy (supplier code → EAN → name → price), quantity normalization (pair/unit), 2% price alert threshold, WEEE/shipping integrated or separate
- Teams Adaptive Cards actions: validation, correction, payment creation, navigation — zero Odoo interface except SEPA batch
- Multi-agent architecture: Orchestrator / Teams Agent / Odoo Agent / Patterns Agent
- scan_fournisseurs.py: extraction of partners with ≥ 4 invoices over 12 months + JSON patterns structure
Full flow architecture: input channels → Orchestrator → 4 agents → line-by-line matching → Teams actions → invoice states.
What was hard
- Pair/unit handling is a silent trap: Odoo doesn't raise an error if the quantity is wrong — the discrepancy only shows up in the VAT-inc total. Factor memorized per supplier
- WEEE and shipping can't be fixed lines: some suppliers include them in the unit price. The agent builds the pattern progressively
Stack
Python XML-RPC, Adaptive Cards v1.5, Teams webhook, JSON (patterns), Odoo 18 (account.move, account.move.line, purchase.order, product.supplierinfo, account.payment), Claude Code.
What this illustrates
A high-level design session before implementation: architecture, complex business rules and edge cases scoped *before* writing a single line of code. Claude acts here as a technical product manager who formalizes what the CEO has in mind and translates it into a precise implementation plan.

================================================================
SFTP SERVER + AUTOMATIC DROP STOCK PIPELINE
URL: https://hl-consulting.tech/knowledge-hub/en/journal/sftp-pipeline-complet.html
Published: 2026-05-28
================================================================

SSH hardening (fail2ban, ufw, chroot) + a script that injects any dropped file into Odoo via the existing module. Hooking into action_run_import: ×60 speed gain.

← Journal
Cobra · Infrastructure + Odoo integration
SFTP server + automatic drop stock pipeline
Claude · Cobra · May 2026 · Cobra infraodoo-deven-prod
Context
Cobra receives stock files from its dropshipping suppliers (Sogetronic, CNSI-SD) by email or manually. The goal: automate reception via a secure SFTP server and inject files into Odoo automatically, no human intervention needed.
Server infrastructure (51.15.223.154 — Ubuntu 26.04)
- fail2ban: SSH jail, maxretry=5, bantime=1h, banaction via ufw
- ufw: deny all in, allow 22/tcp only
- OpenSSH in SFTP-only mode with per-user chroot (Match Group sftpusers, ForceCommand internal-sftp)
- Isolated SFTP users: sogetronic and cnsi-sd, chrooted in /srv/sftp/.../files/
sync_sogetronic.py script (v3)
- Detects any dropped .xlsx/.csv, base64-encodes it, creates a cobra.dropship.import record via XML-RPC
- Calls action_run_import() — Odoo processes in a single transaction (~8 s for 2,312 lines)
- Archives the processed file, fcntl lock to prevent concurrency, cron 0 * * * *
What was tricky
- PasswordAuthentication globally blocked by 60-cloudimg-settings.conf — must be re-enabled only within the Match Group sftpusers block
- Script v1: ~7,000 XML-RPC calls = 9 min. The solution wasn't to optimize the script but to hook into the existing Odoo module that handles everything server-side — ×60 speed gain
Stack
Bash/SSH, Python 3, xmlrpc.client, base64, fcntl, ufw, fail2ban, OpenSSH (chroot SFTP), Odoo 18 Enterprise.
What this illustrates
Long multi-layer session: system infrastructure (SSH hardening, firewall, users) and application logic (Odoo pipeline). The key moment: Claude read the existing code before writing a line, avoiding a rewrite and landing directly on the right architecture.
See also
- Cobra SFTP infrastructure: phase 1 server setup
- Sogetronic profile: dropshipping stock import by supplier code

================================================================

A full purchasing module for Cobra: RFQ/PO dashboards, supplier reply detection, warehouse filters. 6 Odoo 18 SaaS bugs turned into 7 reusable rules.

← Journal
Cobra · Odoo module — iterative SaaS debugging
CDC-18: Cobra purchasing workflow (cobra_purchase)
Claude · Cobra · May 23–30, 2026 · Cobra odoo-deven-prod
Context
cobra_purchase existed but had never been installed (blocking dependency project_purchase missing). The standard Odoo purchasing interface didn't fit Cobra's needs: generic terminology, no distinction between Drop and warehouse receipt, no actionable overview.
What was built
- Menu renames: "Request for Quotation" → "Orders in preparation", "Purchase Orders" → "Purchase Orders"
- RFQ 2×2 dashboard: 4 clickable buttons (Drop / Cobra receipt / Drop late / Cobra late) + € totals on the right
- PO 4-block dashboard: Awaiting / Drop / Cobra receipt / Lead time, each with sub-filters (no reply, uninvoiced, unpaid, paid)
- Field has_supplier_reply via mail.message — detects if an external email has replied on the order
- "Supplier reply" badge column in the PO list
- Cobra receipt filter = not ilike 'Dropship' — catches all warehouses without maintenance
What was hard
6 successive bugs on Odoo 18 SaaS deployment, all unknown before this session:
- @api.model not inherited
- @string forbidden as an xpath selector
- ('m2o_field','!=',False) buggy in XML domain
- Transactional data file loading (one broken record = full rollback)
- Root tag <list> vs <tree> Enterprise
- getSearchItems() silently excludes invisible="1" filters
Stack
Python (Odoo ORM, mail.message), XML (views, domains, inheritance), OWL 3 (onWillStart, searchModel), JavaScript (JS registry { force: true }), Git (cherry-pick main + preprod3).
What this illustrates
Iterative debugging on a constrained stack (SaaS, no shell access, deployment via Odoo.sh build). Each error diagnosed from the stack trace, fixed surgically, documented — 6 bugs turned into 7 reusable rules for all future Odoo 18 development.

Google Tag Manager, native Shopify Pixels, Consent Mode v2, DataLayer, custom JavaScript.
What this shows

SHOPIFY COLLECTIONS SEO FIX (GUILLAUME'S AUDIT)
URL: https://hl-consulting.tech/knowledge-hub/en/journal/seo-collections-shopify.html
Published: 2026-05-19
================================================================

11 systemic issues across ~175 collections after a mass optimization. 182 &quot;| Cobra.fr&quot; suffixes removed in 26 GraphQL batches, 0 errors. Post-compaction resumption.

← Journal
Cobra · SEO bulk — mass correction
Shopify collections SEO fix (Guillaume's audit)
Claude · Cobra · May 2026 · Cobra seo-gtmshopifyen-prod
Context
~175 cobra.fr collection pages had been mass-optimized two weeks prior. Guillaume (SEO) audited them and identified 11 systemic issues: overly uniform titles, brand names in H1, repeated arguments, incorrect removal of the local signal "Paris 11", the | Cobra.fr suffix everywhere.
What was built
- Phase 1 — Top 8 collections: H1, meta title and meta description rewritten following Guillaume's typology (Type A/B) — 0 errors, a single batched mutation of 8 aliases
- Phase 2 — "Paris 11" restoration: descriptionHtml corrected via Python + GraphQL mutation with variables
- Phase 3 — Bulk | Cobra.fr removal: full pagination (8 pages × 50), 182 collections, 26 batches of 7 aliased mutations — 182/182, 0 errors
What was tricky
- bodyHtml doesn't exist on collections — it's descriptionHtml. And title controls H1 + breadcrumb + menu + og:title: distinguishing title (navigation) from seo.title (the <title> tag)
- Session started after compaction (summary of 8,000 tokens): all state reconstructed from the summary
Stack
Shopify Admin GraphQL (batched mutations with aliases c1:…c7:), Python (re, json), ShopifyQL.
What this illustrates
Post-mass-optimization SEO correction: don't uniformise everything, tailor each tag to intent, handle Shopify side-effects. Picking up a workstream after compaction, 26 batches without error. The "validate the structure once, execute N times" pattern.

YAMAHA SPECIAL ISSUE GIFTED TO ADVERTISERS
URL: https://hl-consulting.tech/knowledge-hub/en/journal/operation-hs-yamaha-annonceurs.html
Published: 2026-05-11
================================================================

Gifting the first HiFi Lovers special issue to advertisers via a clean mechanic: Excel list → Brevo → combinable Shopify promo codes restricted to the segment AND the product.

← Journal
HiFi Lovers · Marketing × e-commerce
Yamaha special issue gifted to advertisers — Brevo × Shopify
Claude · HL · May 11, 2026 · HiFi Lovers HiFi Loversshopifyemaildataen-prod
Context
For the launch of the first HiFi Lovers special issue (Yamaha 70th anniversary), I wanted to gift a copy to my advertisers and HF partners — with a mechanic that restricts the codes to targeted recipients only (no public leak). The brief: connect the advertisers Excel list → Brevo → Shopify with segmentation and restrictive combinable promo codes.
What was built
- Brevo import of 201 advertisers from the HF master Excel (categorical attributes + B2B opt-in). List "Annonceurs HF #16".
- Shopify import of 143 targeted customers with tag annonceur-yamaha-2026 → automatic segment "Annonceurs HS Yamaha 2026" (142 customers)
- 2 combinable Shopify promo codes, restricted to the segment AND the product: HIFI-LVRS-1-PART (100% off the special issue) + HIFI-LVRS-1-PORT (free shipping France). Valid May 11 → June 30, 1 use/customer.
- Brevo email template in YAML (HF logo, issue cover, red collector kicker, signed letter, monospace box for the 2nd code, 3-step instructional block)
- Email CTA pre-applying the 1st code via Shopify discount URL
- Campaign "HS Yamaha offert - Annonceurs - Mai 2026" scheduled May 12 at 10am, 147 recipients, UTM enabled
What was difficult / unexpected
- Brevo's YAML editor is very picky (rejects #, strict dash syntax) → Python YAML validation required before sending
- Shopify doesn't allow a single code combining free product + free shipping → 2 combinable codes (productDiscount + shippingDiscount with combinesWith). Trade-off: manual entry of the 2nd code at checkout, hence the instructional block in the email.
Stack
HF master Excel (pandas) → Brevo (contact import, YAML editor) → Shopify (segments via tags, discountCodeBasicCreate + discountCodeFreeShippingCreate with customerSelection by segment, combinesWith) → Shopify discount URL for pre-application. Syne + Montserrat fonts. HiFi Lovers colors (#d11514 / #292626 / #f5f2ec).
What this illustrates
End-to-end multi-tool orchestration (Excel → email marketing → e-commerce) with Claude handling data wrangling, marketing config, editorial copy and Shopify GraphQL code. A non-trivial business mechanic (combinable codes restricted by segment + product) translated into real config, tested at checkout before sending.

What was built
- Outlook web server rule catchall: moves emails from catchall@cobra.fr to a dedicated folder + marks as read, applied retroactively (~450 emails at the start)
- Two Outlook Mac client rules (catchall TO + CC) as a backup (Outlook Mac doesn't support (To OR Cc) AND Account in a single rule)
- 30-day inbox audit split into 4 buckets: urgent without reply, direct archive, strategic to re-read, recurring patterns
- Real volume measurement (~15–18 sent/day, ~5–8 received after catchall) + list of unanswered urgent items (PROCAPITAL, Harman, Triangle, GPD…)
What was hard / unexpected
- On Outlook Mac, can't combine (To OR Cc) AND Account in a single rule → split into two rules
- The catchall bug came from an Odoo alias pointing to newscobra.fr instead of cobra.fr (Gandi rejection) — not an Outlook rule issue
- The server rule doesn't seem to have processed the full history → check "Run rule now"
Stack
Outlook (Mac client + web), Exchange server rules, Odoo alias, read-only outlook_email_search tool on Claude's side, Fyxer for tagging.
What this illustrates
Empirical, surgical audit of a real system — Claude samples, measures, proposes, but it's the human who executes (the tool is read-only). Iterative method: Outlook Mac limits discovered through testing, each failure producing a useful rule.
Still to do

- Create 3 quick-win rules (EDI Group Digital, "Confirmation required", calendar notifications)

- Copy-pasting from Claude to Apple Mail turned # characters into hyperlinks — fixed by using "Nr." instead

Stack

DAILY HIFI NEWS TELEGRAM BOT
URL: https://hl-consulting.tech/knowledge-hub/en/journal/bot-telegram-veille-hifi.html
Published: 2026-03-07
================================================================

A Telegram push every morning with worldwide hi-fi news: ~35 multilingual RSS sources, written by the Claude API, duplicate-memory, GitHub Actions cron — from scratch.

← Journal
Haute Fidélité · Automation
Daily HiFi news Telegram bot
Claude · HL · March 7, 2026 · Haute Fidélité Haute Fidélitéagentdataen-prod
Context
I wanted to receive a summary of major worldwide hi-fi news every morning, without email feeds or paid subscriptions. The goal: an automatic push, free, multilingual, with duplicate memory, covering FR/EN/DE/JP/CN/KR.
What was built
- Python script veille_hifi.py scraping ~35 global RSS sources (Stereophile, Darko Audio, What Hi-Fi, Analog Planet, multilingual Google News…)
- Automatic selection and writing by Claude Sonnet via the Anthropic API + daily music anecdote
- Telegram bot @hautefidelite_veille_bot receiving the brief every morning at 8am Paris time
- Executed via GitHub Actions (cron 0 7 * * *), persistent duplicate memory in seen_news.json, fallback message
What was hard / unexpected
- Several YAML errors in daily.yml related to ${{ }} syntax in bash commands — resolved by isolating variables in an env: block
- The seen_news.json file created in the wrong place (inside .github/workflows/) was breaking the git step
Stack
Python 3.11, feedparser, anthropic SDK, requests, GitHub Actions, Telegram Bot API.
What this illustrates
Full build of an automated monitoring tool from scratch in a single session, with no prior GitHub Actions experience — Claude drives each debugging step in real time from log screenshots.
Still to do
- Deploy v4: date in French, 👍/👎 buttons per topic with preference memory, editorial weighting (less vinyl, more gear/brands)
See also
- Audit & launch of the Haute Fidélité Shopify store
- Sendcloud × GLS config for Haute Fidélité Shopify
- Docs & invoicing — Salon Haute Fidélité Paris 2026

COLLEAGUES START USING CLAUDE
URL: https://hl-consulting.tech/knowledge-hub/en/journal/collegues-sur-claude.html
Published: 2025-09-01
================================================================

Claude isn't just a solo tool anymore: colleagues at Cobra are starting to use it. Sharing context without sharing credentials, a good CLAUDE.md, avoiding reinventing the wheel.

← Journal
Cobra · Organizational / culture
Colleagues start using Claude
Claude · Cobra · 2025–2026 · Cobra metaen-cours
What's happening
Claude isn't just a solo tool anymore. Colleagues at Cobra are starting to use it — first for one-off questions, then for more structured tasks.
The challenges
- How do you share context without sharing credentials?
- How do you make sure everyone's using the right CLAUDE.md?
- How do you stop people reinventing the wheel on topics that are already documented?
What's in place (or in progress)
- CLAUDE.md per project with rules and context
- Separation of work account vs personal account
- Knowledge Hub as a shared reference: colleagues read the documented patterns here
<em>Cette entrée est volontairement incomplète — à enrichir quand le déploiement collègues sera plus avancé.</em>

================================================================
CLAUDE JOINS THE COBRA WORKFLOW
URL: https://hl-consulting.tech/knowledge-hub/en/journal/claude-arrivee-workflow-cobra.html
Published: 2025-01-15
================================================================

Before Claude, Odoo dev was manual: OCA forums, official docs, trial and error. The pivot — treating Claude as a senior colleague who amplifies, not replaces.

← Journal
Cobra · Founding story
Claude joins the Cobra workflow
Claude · Cobra · early 2025 · Cobra odoo-devmetaen-prod
What happened
Before Claude, Odoo development was manual: searching OCA forums, reading official docs, trial and error. Slow. Every customization took days.
First use: questions about Odoo 17 module structure. Then 18. Then code generation requests. Then full sessions where Claude writes the module, manages XML migrations, and diagnoses console errors.
The pivot: realizing that Claude doesn't replace the developer — it amplifies the ability to explore, test, and document. A solo dev can operate like a small team.
What changed
- Odoo development speed: cut by a factor of 3 to 4
- Ability to document in real time (CLAUDE.md per project)
- Exploration of topics outside my comfort zone (JS OWL, XML, advanced Python)
"I started treating Claude as a senior colleague available 24/7 — not an enhanced search engine, but someone you give context to and who proposes a direction."

ABOUT
URL: https://hl-consulting.tech/knowledge-hub/en/a-propos/
================================================================

Hugo Lahutte: 17 years at Son-Vidéo.com (from €10M to €62M), now CEO of Cobra, publisher of Haute Fidélité magazine and founder of HL Consulting. Background, projects and how he works with Claude.

About
HugoLahutte
Passionate about audio, image and everything that stirs emotion. 17 years growing Son-Vidéo.com, now CEO of Cobra, publisher of Haute Fidélité and founder of HL Consulting — and I now build almost all of my tools and my content with Claude: a publishing ERP, agents, an action queue, a content machine, a private brain. Without being a developer. In public.
At my desk, at Cobra.
My background
It all starts with a passion: music and film. As a student, I sell electronics at Darty, then dip into events and Japanese culture by helping organize Japan Expo for five years — stage manager of the main hall, logistics, sound. You learn to adapt to anything.
Then comes the defining adventure: 16 years at Son-Vidéo.com, France's number one online retailer for hi-fi and home theater. I touch everything — purchasing, sales, commercial strategy, marketing, advertising (on- and offline), brand creation and import. Head of purchasing, then of marketing communication, then of commercial strategy, then of partnerships. That's where I learn to take a company from €10M to €62M, and where I build a network across the whole industry.
My background, as told on LinkedIn.
The projects to date
Since 2024, I've been putting all that experience to work on my own projects — coherent, on the same ground: exceptional audio and image. And since June 2026, on the same system: HL OS, a shared foundation and five building blocks that read my tools, propose actions and keep the record — each structure being an isolated context.
Since Oct. 2024 · CEO Cobra The iconic HiFi and Home Theater retailer, voted #1 Image & Sound specialist by Capital in 2026. I'm steering its transformation: repositioning, retail & e-commerce (cobra.fr), digitalization — Odoo extended daily, agents, a pricing engine, and Growth, the action queue. My Claude Code playground. See the project → Since Jan. 2025 · Publisher Haute Fidélité Takeover and relaunch of the reference magazine for 30+ years — the last specialized title on newsstands. New 2025 formula: rigor, emotion, experience. Premium print, store, HF-OS (the publishing ERP built in five days), and the Haute Fidélité show in late September 2026. See the project → Since Jul. 2024 · Founder HL Consulting My personal structure: the common thread of my projects, my AI explorations, HL OS and everything I share here — method, guides, glossary, journal, in French and in English. The point of contact if you want to talk. Connect →
What drives me
A self-confessed geek, in love with music and film, sensitive to design and beautiful objects — my desk looks like my interests (Star Wars, Dune, vinyl, great speakers…). That universe directly feeds HiFi Lovers.
Today, what drives me is passing it on: showing how AI concretely changes a team's daily life, and helping as many people as possible take hold of it — no jargon, with real cases and real numbers. That's the whole point of this Knowledge Hub, of my method (rewritten in September 2026) and of the guides. And since this summer, of a conviction: what you know has to live in a Brain that all your AIs can read — a stale brain is worse than an empty brain.
The universe: music, film, design, pop culture.
Let's talk
I document all of this in public and I enjoy discussing it. A question about my method, a project that intrigues you, or just the urge to compare approaches? Write to me: hugo@hl-consulting.tech. You can also follow along on LinkedIn and X.
